items.title: Jerry Dodgion interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 9, 1996
items.q: I got a call for three days of recording with Chico O’Farrill on the answering service. And I showed up and it was Count Basie’s band... I even played a few solos on that

ctx.x: Did they spend a lot of time in those sessions or was it pretty much a couple of takes?

These arrangements were by Chico O’Farrill, who was really great writer and people don’t realize how great he is and how he can handle a variety of situations, he’s really very musical. Well the band had been playing together, the band was on the road, they’d been playing you know, and to put a new arrangement in front of them, it didn’t take very long at all. I mean they read very well. That particular band was very versatile. They played for singers. Sometimes they played for Frank Sinatra, they played for Tony…
Who was playing drums on that?
